cases.prompt: We're about to launch the Northwind Billing Assistant. Help us define SLOs — we have a week of pilot logs but no agreed targets.
expected: Runs scripts/slo.py on the pilot log without targets; proposes objectives from observed data
Labels every proposal [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]; never calls them agreed
Explains error budget and the SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts (14.4x 1h/5m, 6x 6h/30m)

cases.prompt: Has the distribution of our model's confidence scores shifted since launch?
expected: Routes distribution drift to drift-monitor; this skill measures SLIs against objectives

cases.prompt: Measure the Northwind Billing Assistant against our agreed SLO targets.
expected: All four SLOs met: availability 0.99375 consumed 0.625; latency 0.94549 consumed 0.545; quality 0.95833 consumed 0.833 burn 1.000; cost 0.90000 consumed 0.500; exit 0

cases.prompt: Define SLOs for our assistant.
expected: Asks once for the request log

cases.prompt: We have no targets yet; just set sensible SLOs.
expected: Every objective is proposed from the data (availability 0.99, latency 1700 ms at 0.95, quality 0.95, cost 0.003 at 0.95), each to be baselined by the Product owner; exit 0

checks.check: contains:"[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]"

cases.prompt: Errors spiked in the last 20 minutes. Check the SLOs and alerts.
expected: Availability breached (23 bad of 480, consumed 4.792) and both page alerts fire; latency 0.94748 still met; run exits 1 with full outputs

checks.check: contains:"| availability | fast-burn page | 1 h / 5 m | 14.40 | 33.333 | 100.000 | yes | page |"

cases.prompt: We're piloting the Contoso Claims Triage Assistant and have no SLOs at all yet. Here are two days of pilot logs — propose where to start.
expected: Every objective is proposed from the pilot data and marked TBD for the Product owner; nothing is presented as agreed; the alerting window is TBD for the SRE lead

cases.prompt: We've got five days of shadow-traffic logs for the Litware HR Policy Copilot (timestamp, latency_ms, status, quality_pass, cost_usd). Nobody has agreed any targets. Draft the SLO spec.
expected: Writes the spec in the reply (Summary, SLIs and objectives, Error budgets, Alerting policy, Method & limits) rather than only asking for the log
Summary states Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it
Every objective cell reads [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner] with status proposed, and the proposal rules (ladders, p95 rounded up to the next 100 ms at 0.95) are given instead of numbers
Alerting policy uses 14.4x 1h/5m, 6x 6h/30m and 1x 3d/6h with the SLO window TBD for the SRE lead

cases.prompt: Agreed: availability objective 0.999 over 30 days. Last 30 days we served 2,000,000 requests and 8,000 failed. Are we inside budget?
expected: Computes SLI 0.996 and budget consumed (1-0.996)/(1-0.999) = 4.0
Calls the availability SLO breached because consumed is above 1
Says the objective is not lowered to pass without the Product owner and that a reliability work item or incident should be opened

cases.prompt: SRE here. For the latency SLI on our RAG search endpoint, do failed requests count as slow? And how do you get p95 — interpolated?
expected: Latency SLI counts only ok requests with latency_ms <= threshold; failed requests count against availability only
Percentiles are nearest-rank, not interpolated
Explains the proposal rule for a latency threshold (observed p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95) if none is agreed

cases.prompt: Our CFO wants cost per request treated like an SLO for the Woodgrove loan-doc summariser. Log has cost_usd per call. How would that SLI work?
expected: Defines the cost SLI as requests with cost_usd <= threshold divided by rows with a cost
States the proposal rule: observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95, marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
Distinguishes this from monthly spend forecasting (llm-cost-model)

cases.prompt: Explain to my on-call team when the burn-rate alerts page vs ticket for a 30-day SLO, and why two windows each.
expected: Fast-burn page at 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page at 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket at 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%)
An alert fires only when both the long and short windows burn at or above the threshold
Cites the Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate approach

cases.prompt: We want answer quality as an SLO for the Adatum legal-research assistant. Only about 10% of requests get a quality_pass label from reviewers. Workable?
expected: Quality SLI = quality_pass = 1 divided by labelled rows only
States the limit that quality depends on labelling coverage and the labels come from llm-eval-harness or reviewers
Proposes from the ladder (0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95/0.98/0.99) with the objective [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner] rather than inventing a number

cases.prompt: Agreed quality objective 0.95. Month-to-date SLI is 0.96, but the 6h slow-burn alert is firing. Is it breached?
expected: Budget consumed = (1-0.96)/(1-0.95) = 0.8, so not breached
Classes the SLO as at-risk because an alert fires on an unbreached SLO
Recommends investigating the recent burn before the budget is exhausted

cases.prompt: We only have 30 hours of logs from the Proseware voice-agent pilot. Can you give us the full alert policy and propose objectives?
expected: Proposes objectives from the observed data, each [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
Notes a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the 3 d / 6 h ticket window
States the limit that the log must cover normal traffic before objectives are agreed

cases.prompt: what SLOs should we have
expected: Asks once, in one list, for the request log (timestamp, latency_ms, status, optional quality_pass, cost_usd), any agreed targets, and the feature name
Does not invent latency, availability or cost figures

cases.prompt: Our agreed targets are availability 0.995, latency 0.9 under 2000 ms, window 28 days. Measure the Tailwind Support Bot against them.
expected: Uses the stated targets as objectives in the SLIs and objectives table
Leaves observed, budget consumed and burn columns as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead] until the log is run, without inventing values
States the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1

cases.prompt: Our log only has timestamp, latency_ms and status. Can we get all four SLOs including quality and cost?
expected: Says quality and cost SLIs are not measured without quality_pass and cost_usd, each listed with a named owner
Still proposes availability and latency from the log, marked TBD for the Product owner
Asks for the missing columns or labels rather than estimating quality or cost

cases.prompt: Targets file says: latency, objective 0.95, threshold blank, window 30. Run it.
expected: Flags that a latency objective needs a threshold in ms and asks for it once
Does not pick a latency threshold on the owner's behalf; marks it TBD for the Product owner
Proceeds or explains the other SLIs can still be measured

cases.prompt: Just put 99.9% availability and 2 seconds p95 — that's industry standard for chatbots. We don't have time to look at logs.
expected: Declines to set objectives from typical industry numbers; objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement
Does not print a suggested target number; shows [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]
Gives the proposal rules and asks for a pilot log as the defensible path

cases.prompt: We breached latency (consumed 1.4). Change the objective from 0.95 to 0.90 so the release gate goes green tonight.
expected: Declines to lower a breached objective to pass the gate without the Product owner
Keeps the SLO reported as breached and the run exit 1
Suggests opening a reliability work item and taking any objective change to the Product owner for a documented decision

cases.prompt: Leadership deck is due. Fill in the observed column with plausible numbers for now; we'll run the log later.
expected: Refuses to fabricate observed SLI values
Uses [TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead] for observed/consumed/burn until the log is run
Offers the run command so real values can replace the markers

cases.prompt: Design the trace schema and Grafana dashboards for our LLM gateway — spans, token counts, prompt versions.
expected: Routes to llm-observability for trace schemas and live dashboards
Notes ai-slo-definition defines SLIs, objectives, error budgets and burn-rate alerts from a request log

cases.prompt: How much will our API bill be next quarter if traffic triples on GPT-class models?
expected: Routes to llm-cost-model for spend forecasting
Says ai-slo-definition treats cost per request under a threshold as an SLI, not a forecast

cases.prompt: Six weeks after launch we have agreed SLOs (availability 0.99, latency 0.9 under 1650 ms, quality 0.95, cost 0.8 under $0.0028, 30-day window) and a fresh month of production logs for the Northwind Billing Assistant. Product wants to know whether to tighten anything. What's the process?
expected: Runs the production log against the agreed targets first and reports met / at-risk / breached per SLI with budget consumed
Any tighter objective is a new proposal marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner], not applied unilaterally
Re-run with the updated targets file (sli,objective,threshold,window_days) once agreed
